Maria: Heads-up — ran the nightly small-batch decode sweep and saw a consistent p99/p95 regression when FlashFusedV2 + KVPage are enabled on small continuous decode workloads.
Maria: Batch_size=1, seq_len=16, steady-state traffic, p99 jump ~30% compared to FlashPagedX baseline.
Ajay: ugh. Any logs or profiler output?
Maria: Paste of the minimal repro run:
Maria: ```
./bench_runner --model=redwood-13b --mode=decode --batch_size=1 --seq_len=16 --kernel=FlashFusedV2 --kv_mode=KVPage --continuous=true --iters=2000
# metrics: p50=18ms p95=42ms p99=64ms
# baseline (FlashPagedX): p50=17ms p95=33ms p99=49ms
```
Lee: That's a pretty big tail gap. Do you see GPU kernels stalling or extra memcpy?
Maria: NVTX traces show extra kernel launches during decode steps that correspond to KV page compaction work. Timeline snippet: there are frequent small memcpy D->D around KVPage::compact() that serialize the decode stream.
Maria: Quick nvprof snippet (summed over 1s window):
Maria: ```
Kernel                                Calls  Total(ms)  Avg(ms)
flash_fused_attn_v2                    1200    3100     2.58
kvpage_compact                         900     820      0.91
kv_cache_lookup                        2400    480      0.20
memcpy_device_to_device                1800    250      0.14
```
Ajay: Interesting that kvpage_compact is that heavy. Could be fragmentation threshold running too aggressively for small decode where kv entries are tiny.
Kim: On small-batch decode we usually avoid compaction because it hurts streaming latency. What config flips do we have?
Maria: There's a runtime flag currently in canary: --kvpage-compact-threshold=0.6 (fraction of pages to trigger compaction). When we lowered to 0.2 the compaction rate dropped but p95 still worse by ~10% vs baseline.
Lee: Maybe kernel selection is picking FlashFusedV2 which has more expensive prologue for small sequence lengths. Could be warmup / prologue setup cost dominating when continuous batching makes many micro-decoder calls.
Ajay: Can you compare kernel time per token for prefill vs decode? I want to see per-step overhead.
Maria: Prefill vs decode per-token median: prefill ~0.9ms/token, decode ~0.6ms/token baseline. With FlashFusedV2 decode median 0.7ms/token but decode has extra 0.9ms per-step overhead when KVPage compact fires. So per-step overhead matters because decode is small-batch.
Kim: Two hypotheses: 1) FlashFusedV2 has a higher fixed setup cost for each decode invocation that doesn't amortize at batch_size=1; 2) KVPage compaction interacts poorly with continuous batching leading to serialization.
Lee: Agreed. We should try two experiments in parallel: A) force kernel to FlashPagedX for a canary to see if p99 drops; B) switch KVPage compaction to async (background) or increase the page granularity (bigger pages -> fewer compactions).
Maria: I ran A locally — forcing FlashPagedX drops p99 back to ~50ms, same as baseline. So kernel selection matters a lot.
Ajay: Good. For B, we have an experimental flag --kvpage-compact-async that offloads compaction to a background stream; curious if that reduces tail.
Maria: Tried async compaction: p99 improved but p95 still ~10% worse. Looks like compaction isn't the only factor.
Kim: Could be that the fused kernel path (FlashFusedV2) optimizes the prefill case better but pays a penalty per decode call due to extra pointer setup for KV pointers. We should inspect the prologue assembly for small seq lengths.
Lee: Also check continuous batching layer: when we hit KVPage compact we might block the batching thread which stops other in-flight micro-batches merging. That would increase effective latency beyond just compaction time.
ops-bot: Canary: deploy flagged kernels FlashFusedV2=on to 10% edge; KVPage compact async=off to 100% started by maria at 2167654350
Ajay: Can we instrument the batching queue depth and blocking times? That will show whether compaction pauses the scheduler.
Maria: Added two more probes to the microbatch scheduler to log queue stalls >5ms. Ran for 30k queries: saw ~700 stalls, 92% of them aligned with kvpage_compact events.
Maria: Log example: 
Maria: ```
[2167654301.124] microbatch: enqueue (id=1234) depth=0
[2167654301.125] microbatch: stall start reason=kvpage_compact id=1234
[2167654301.140] microbatch: stall end duration=15ms
```
Lee: 15ms stall explains a lot. If these are frequent, they cascade. For small-batch decode, you can't hide a 15ms stall.
Kim: Short-term fix: 1) Add heuristic to avoid compaction when batch_size<=2 and continuous=true. 2) Force kernel selection to FlashPagedX for batch_size<=1 until we optimize prologue cost.
Ajay: Long-term: 1) Move compaction async and ensure it doesn't steal compute stream used by decode; 2) Reduce fused-kernel prologue overhead for small seqs or add a fast-path microkernel for decode step.
Maria: I'll open a PR with canary config changes: disable kvpage compaction under small-batch continuous, and add a kernel selection rule mapping small decode -> FlashPagedX. Will include perf numbers.
Kim: Assign to Maria for quick canary, Lee to investigate fused prologue assembly, Ajay to prototype async compaction without stream contention.
Maria: Plan: canary rollback if p99 not reduced within 30m. I scheduled a canary run on staging for 2167654365.
Lee: Thanks — also let's capture a short trace with CUPTI for one of the stalls so we have exact kernel stack.
Ajay: I'll follow up with an automated micro-bench that reproduces the stall deterministically (seed traffic pattern).
Maria: Cool. TL;DR: small-batch decode tail regression caused by combination of FlashFusedV2 prologue cost + KVPage compaction blocking batching scheduler. Canary changes in flight.
Kim: :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Canary update: canary run healthy metrics at 5m mark, p99 for stage reduced by ~22% after kernel override at 2167654380
Maria: Will post bench artifacts and flamegraphs to the thread in 1 hour.
Lee: Nice work, big win if we can avoid perf cliff for small decode users.
